REGISTERED (primary archive, R-129's 512 frozen-JOINT cases at 1.5x): success in the highest transverse-displacement quartile minus the lowest, standardized over all nine axial x tilt strata (full common support): -0.056, 95% interval [-0.177, +0.064]. It spans both zero and -0.15: INCONCLUSIVE. The predeclared separate replication (R-133's 1,536 frozen-JOINT cases at 1.5x): -0.172 [-0.239, -0.105], a clear deficit whose interval still spans -0.15, so the registered magnitude is not established there either; the two archives are not pooled. NOT REGISTERED, descriptive, identical in both archives: the failures track the pen's initial TILT far more than its displacement. Success by tilt quartile (lowest to highest): 0.812 / 0.594 / 0.383 / 0.156 in R-129 and 0.815 / 0.526 / 0.326 / 0.182 in R-133; by transverse quartile 0.516 / 0.531 / 0.453 / 0.445 and 0.523 / 0.503 / 0.456 / 0.367; by axial quartile it is flat (0.43-0.56 and 0.43-0.52). So at 1.5x resets the frozen JOINT keeps its nominal success (about 0.8) on the least-tilted quarter of cases and fails five times in six on the most-tilted quarter; the wide-reset weakness of D-089 is mostly an initial-orientation effect. This was not the registered hypothesis and is an association over reconstructed geometry; it needs its own prospective test before it is relied on.
